## 0.9.4.25 — D9b (Candidate B) failure record

**Recorded as a failure, not a success.** The run of evidence-based
refutations continues.

Hypothesis: removing duplicated buffer/SSIM preparation in the expensive
verify path will reduce cost.
Result: **not one counter changed, and no time reduction either.**

The cause is now established by measurement. Per-call work:

```
frame_ssim        20 calls x 4,096 inner loop = 81,920 ops  <- all of it
centerCropResize   8 calls x 1,024 pixels     =  8,192 ops  <- D9b removed 2,048
```

D9b touched only **2.3 %** of the work and never reduced any of the
81,920 `frame_ssim` ops. Further, **the duplication the hypothesis pointed at
did not exist in the original** — it already computed each aspect buffer once
outside the loop.

### What this session reconfirms

- **Hypotheses must be measured.** D9a refuted the cache-32 hypothesis, and
  D9b refuted the "remove duplication" hypothesis. Twice in a row, code
  review alone could not identify the bottleneck.
- **Separate observation from inference.** "9 of 10 are aspect combinations"
  was a correct **observation**, but "that is the bottleneck" was a **wrong
  inference**. An observation does not automatically imply cost.
- **A safe but useless change is still a failure.** Parity held and every test
  passed, but the success condition (cost reduction) was not met, so it is NOT
  ACCEPTED.

### Remaining directions

- Reducing `frame_ssim` itself can change results, so it needs its own
  pre-register
- Candidate A stays deferred — verdict semantics risk

## 0.9.4.26 — D9c internal cost accounting (instrumentation)

**D9b's failure cause is now established by measurement.**

D9b failed on the hypothesis that buffer recomputation in the scoring path was
the bottleneck. D9c answered with measurement, not a hypothesis.

```text
expensive verify = 8.564 ms

decode             94.90 %   <- the real bottleneck
frame_ssim          0.55 %   <- what D9b optimized
```

`frame_ssim` was the stage D9b estimated as "essentially all of it". It is
actually 0.047 ms. Decode is 173x more expensive than that.

### The lesson from the third repetition

Measurement has now refuted three hypotheses on this development line.

```text
D9a  "verify cache 32 is the bottleneck"     -> refuted
D9b  "duplicated work in the scoring path"   -> refuted
D9c  measure -> decode is 94.90 %            -> established
```

D9a and D9b both *inferred* the bottleneck by reading code. D9b even restructured
code that was already reusing its buffers. In both cases the observation was
right ("9 of 10 are aspect combinations", "same buffer repeatedly") and the
inference that it was the cost was wrong.

**Recurring pattern: observed operation count is not the bottleneck.** Inferring
a bottleneck from an operation-count proxy has now failed three times in a row.
Future bottleneck hypotheses must include an observational measurement in their
pre-register.

### What this build leaves behind

- The answer: 94.90 % of expensive verify cost is image decode.
- D9a's derived "~8.5 ms" is now directly measured at 8.564 ms.
- Left unmeasured rather than estimated: `frame_ssim` internals, decode internals.
- Two structural facts the counters exposed: each miss decodes the same file
  twice, and cache hits still read and hash 64 KiB (363.3 MB).
- Integrity: all counters and groups 156,152 identical to D9a; parity 25 and
  instrumentation checks PASS.

### Next

**Candidate D — image decode cost.** It must first decompose the 4.31 ms decode
into factory/decoder setup, file open, EXIF, Fant scale, format conversion, and
copy. D9c measured decode as a single region. No optimizing without measuring
first; that is exactly how D9b failed.

## 0.9.4.26 — D9d decode internal decomposition (measurement)

D9c measured decode as a single 94.90 % region. This decomposed what is inside
it.

```text
decode 4.4654 ms/call
  open    62.15 %   file open + decoder construction
  factory 27.39 %   per-call WIC factory COM construction
  copy     5.15 %   the actual image decompression
  rest     5.31 %
```

**What this measurement refuted.** The fourth on this line.

```text
D9a  "cache 32 is the bottleneck"        -> refuted
D9b  "duplicated scoring work"           -> refuted
D9c  "decode is the bottleneck"          -> established (94.90%)
D9d  "Fant / EXIF are the cost in decode" -> refuted (0.32% / 0.17%)
```

`WICBitmapInterpolationModeFant` sounds expensive because it is the
high-quality interpolation mode, and it is 0.32 %. The EXIF metadata query is
0.17 %. The side that does not show up in the name -- file open and COM factory
construction -- is 89.55 %. And the actual decompression that "decode is
expensive" intuition points at is 5.15 %, a twentieth of the cost.

### A second refutation, about the mutex

D9c left open the possibility that the verify cache's global mutex causes
contention. D9d measured it.

```text
wait 0.0002 ms/acquire    hold 0.0018 ms/acquire
total lock time = 0.07 % of decode
```

It is not a bottleneck, and that is now settled by measurement rather than
assumption. It also confirms there is no hidden contention inside D9c's `other`
bucket (0.42 %).

### The cumulative lesson of this line

Four times in a row, a bottleneck hypothesis built by reading code has been
overturned by measurement. D9d's contribution is not to stop that repetition
but to **cut it short with evidence.** Fant and EXIF are now excluded by
measurement rather than by ignorance, and "look at this next" has been narrowed
to "decompose the 2.77 ms open and the 1.22 ms factory first."

Good measurement does not only answer questions. It also **deletes** them. The
question that did not exist before, "is the mutex a problem," is now closed by
measurement, and the question that did exist, "which part of decode," narrowed
from one region to two.

### Next

Candidate D1 -- image decoder construction and file open. It must first
decompose the internals of `open` and `factory`, and check whether the
`CLSID_WICImagingFactory2` attempt is failing and falling back. If it is
falling back, the fast path is not being taken at all, and that outranks
everything else.

Not implemented here. Optimizing without measuring is what caused the repeated
failures on this line.

## 0.9.4.27 — D1: why file open and factory are expensive

D9d measured `open + factory` at 89.55 % of decode and 84.93 % of the verify,
but not what was inside. This answered two questions.

```text
Question B: does Factory2 work?
  attempts 25,898 / successes 25,898 (100%) / fallbacks 0

Question A: where does the 2.6 ms of open go?
  OS CreateFileW        0.0576 ms  (2.2%)
  WIC internal          2.5682 ms  (97.8%)
```

### Two things were deleted

The largest output of this build is not "what to optimize" but **what not to.**

1. **Removing the Factory2 fallback** — **zero** fallbacks in 25,898 calls.
   There is nothing to remove on this machine. The "the first attempt is
   wasted" hypothesis was refuted by measurement.
2. **File handle / stream management optimization** — the real OS cost is
   0.0576 ms, 2.2 % of `open`. The cost was not opening the file; it was WIC
   constructing a decoder. The name "file open" was misleading.

Both are candidates that names and intuition pull in naturally. Had either gone
unmeasured, both would have been implemented, and both would have done nothing.

### Measurement caught a measurement bug

The first implementation reported `factoryMs = 235,023,895 ms` -- an impossible
figure for a ~2 minute workload. The shared helper accumulates into **running
totals**, and the call site added those totals again on every call, so the sum
grew quadratically.

The pre-register's "stop if the split does not reconstruct factoryMs" caught it
exactly. Without that identity check, and with buckets less obviously broken, a
plausible-looking but wrong set of percentages would have been reported.

**Accounting is a precondition of a measurement, not a finishing touch.**

### The cumulative pattern (sixth build on this line)

```text
D9a  "cache 32"          -> refuted
D9b  "duplicated scoring" -> refuted
D9c  decode found        -> established
D9d  Fant / EXIF         -> refuted
D1   "Factory2 fallback"  -> refuted (0 occurrences)
D1   "file open"          -> partly refuted (OS is 2.2 %)
```

This approach keeps producing new candidates, but more often it **deletes**
existing ones. Deleting is the more valuable half. A deleted candidate does not
come back; a surviving wrong one keeps costing.

## 2026-09-30 — Benchmark / Console CLI Design Addition

The existing GUI already separates benchmark scope by image/video selection, so Console must expose the same independent axis.

### Decision

- Benchmark mode: AUTO / CPU-only / GPU-max
- Media scope: images / videos / all
- Console canonical option: --media images|videos|all
- GUI media selection and Console --media must represent the same source-file scope
- GUI: retain only the latest three mode JSON files per source folder
- Console: cumulative retention
- Run / Suite separation
- Normal Search Index and Benchmark index/cache isolation
- Run JSON stores mode + mediaScope + dataset identity + environment + scheduler configuration
- GPU-max is not GPU-only; mandatory CPU work and fallback remain enabled

### Implementation order

S0 → S1 → S2 → S3 → S4 → S5 → S6 → S7 → S8

Detailed stages and storage layout are recorded in docs/architecture/benchmark-telemetry-roadmap.*.

This is a **design decision and implementation schedule entry**, not a benchmark performance result. When actual benchmark performance experiments begin, the existing pre-register-first rule applies.

## 2026-09-30 — Final Benchmark Console Execution / UI Decision

The benchmark execution unit and Console presentation model are finalized before implementation.

### Decisions

1. **File-level execution**
   - Run AUTO -> CPU -> GPU-max for one file, persist the file result immediately, then move to the next file.
   - File identification/input preparation may be shared; analytical/decode/intermediate results are not shared across modes.

2. **Cancellation safety**
   - Ctrl+C is a cancellation request.
   - Completed file/mode records must already be persisted so an interrupted process leaves a usable partial Suite.

3. **CPU Resource Policy**
   - Reuse the existing Maximum/High/Balanced/Gaming/Manual 10-90 policy.
   - Recommended default Console benchmark resource is Balanced 55%.
   - Do not turn a linear extrapolation from Balanced into a measured Maximum benchmark result.

4. **Terminal UI**
   - Compress the fixed header to three information rows.
   - Place Target/Scope/IMG+VID progress, Mode/CPU/GPU, and Distance/Suite ID/Build/Git side-by-side.
   - Never auto-wrap the fixed header; use middle ellipsis for long Target paths on screen only.
   - Keep detailed file name/status/time/backend/fallback information in CURRENT FILE below.
   - Keep completed history compact, one line per file.

5. **Data vs view**
   - The terminal is a view; journal/summary is canonical data.
   - Interactive and non-interactive outputs differ only in rendering and use the same data model.

### Preservation

Existing benchmark source/schema remains a permanent legacy benchmark reference. The v0.9.4.43 tag/source backup and existing benchmark records stay as the comparison baseline for the new architecture.

This entry is a design decision, not a benchmark performance result. The existing pre-register-first rule remains mandatory for actual performance experiments.

## 2026-10-01 — S6 Grouping design decision

### Why a single composite grouping key was not adopted

The leading candidate was one key combining `datasetFingerprint + mediaScope +
buildVersion + gitCommit + requestedMode + effectiveMode`. It is the simplest thing
to implement and produces a very short report. **It also puts every run in a cohort
of its own and makes cross-build comparison structurally impossible.** Two runs over
the same dataset and scope but different builds land in different cohorts, so a
later question of "what changed under the same conditions" finds an empty population.

It looks tidier than it is, and what it actually does is delete the comparison, so it
was rejected. This is expensive to reverse once a later stage depends on it, which is
why the reasoning is recorded here.

What was adopted instead is **separate typed keys per analysis axis**. Each axis
answers only its own question, and the caller selects the view it needs. Combining two
keys is the caller's business, not the data layer's.

| View | Key | Question it answers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DatasetCohortKey` | `datasetFingerprint` | Observing one dataset across builds and modes |
| `ScopeCohortKey` | fingerprint + `mediaScope` | The baseline population for cross-build observation |
| `BuildCohortKey` | `buildVersion` + `gitCommitState` + `gitCommit` | Which runs came from the same build |
| `ModeCohortKey` | `requestedMode` + `effectiveMode` | Fallback and capability observations |
| `CaseCohortKey` | fingerprint + `caseId` | Per-file comparison |

### `caseId` is not run-scoped (measured)

S2 derives `caseId` as `IndexManager::folderId(file.path)`, a double FNV-1a hash of the
canonical path. The brief assumed this value was run-scoped, but **measurement shows
the same file in two runs yields the same `caseId`** — two runs over one file produced
the same value. Per-file comparison across runs was therefore always possible. It is
still not trusted alone: it is paired with the dataset fingerprint, because it hashes
an absolute path and could in principle collide across datasets. No new hash was
invented, honouring the brief.

### Legacy / Unknown provenance is never merged into one group

`gitCommit` existing in the journal is not the same as being comparable by commit.
`BuildCohortKey` carries the commit value **and** the provenance state, so Known,
Unknown and Legacy cohorts are separated structurally, and `commitComparable` is true
only for Known. Two Unknown runs are not evidence of the same binary, so the flag
makes them excludable from commit-level comparison. Legacy has no field at all and is
never filled in with the current HEAD. `commitComparable` states **provenance
quality** and is not a comparability verdict.

### What the real journals showed

- **60 records have `requested=CUDA` but `effective=CPU`.** They carry
  `status=SKIPPED` and `errorMessage="mode unavailable in this environment"` — a
  fallback on a machine without GPU support. Had requested and effective been merged,
  60 CUDA observations would have been disguised as CPU runs and the entire
  capability observation would have vanished. Brief §9's reason for keeping them apart
  is confirmed by real data.
- **`all` is the dominant scope** (21 of 31 runs). Not decomposing it into
  images+videos is correct.
- **Build diversity is insufficient** (2 cohorts, 1 commit). Per brief §23 this is
  recorded as normal, and no diversity was fabricated.
- **`suite-ORDER-A/B/C` are fixtures** left in the real benchmark store by S2/S5
  ordering tests. Each journal holds three `run_started` records with the same
  `runId` and duplicated `mode_result` lines. `ModeCohort` counts (run, case, mode)
  as a **set**, so a duplicated record counts once (486 against 494 raw lines). These
  fixtures predate S6 and were not created by it. Separating fixture management from
  the real store may be needed at a later stage.

### Scope

This stage computes membership, counts and provenance only. mean, median, p95, delta,
speedup, failure rate, thresholds, anomalies, final comparability judgement, CLI and
GUI are all **not implemented**, and the journal schema is unchanged. Statistics were
deliberately left out: adding them now would let a later threshold design inherit
unmeasured assumptions.
## 2026-10-01 — S6 Aggregation design decision

### `all` is never decomposed into images/videos

In the real store `all` is 22 of 31 runs. Converting it to `images + videos` would make
the aggregates look tidier, but **the journal does not record how many cases of each
scope an `all` run actually covered.** Distributing the elapsed time therefore requires
inventing a ratio. `all` stays an independent scope and donates no elapsed time to the
others. A later stage makes the user pick `images-only`, `videos-only` or `all`
explicitly.

### SKIPPED / FAILED / CANCELLED are excluded from the performance population

The 60 real `requested=CUDA` / `effective=CPU` / `SKIPPED` /
`mode unavailable in this environment` records are **not CPU performance
observations.** Averaging them would disguise a machine that cannot use the GPU as CPU
speed and would actively distort the capability observation. Rewriting `SKIPPED` as 0 ms
is worse still: it asserts "measured, and the value was zero", inventing a value the
data does not contain.

So all three are **excluded from performance statistics** and **always kept in the
status tally**. Every exclusion carries its reason
(`skipped`/`failed`/`cancelled`/`missingElapsed`/`invalid`). A bare excluded count is
not acceptable, because it cannot be told apart from a bug.

The per-level rules differ, because the model does. mode `elapsedMs` is optional, so a
`Success` with no duration is possible and becomes `missingElapsed`. case `elapsedMs` is
a non-optional `double`, so that case **cannot occur** there and status alone decides. A
run with no terminal record has no status at all, so it is excluded as `invalid` rather
than assumed Success.

### Logical entities, not raw journal duplicates, are aggregated

The real store's `suite-ORDER-A/B/C` wrote the same journal more than once. Averaging raw
lines would weight a repeatedly-written suite above an identical one written once, so
aggregation uses the logical entities S6-1/S6-2 recovered.

> **This surfaced a real defect.** `suite-ORDER-A/B/C` share one `runId`, so **31
> accepted runs carry only 29 distinct runIds.** Keying per-file aggregation on `runId`
> alone kept one of the three and silently dropped the other two runs' cases (case
> observations rose from 314 to 324 once fixed). Deduplicating instead would discard
> measurements in the opposite direction. **The journal cannot say whether these are one
> measurement written three times or three separate measurements**, so neither is applied
> silently: per-file populations are keyed on `(sourceJournalPath, runId)` and the
> collision is only reported through `runsWithCollidingIdentity`.
>
> S6-1 reported "31 accepted" without this being visible, so the point is recorded here:
> **no S6 layer may assume runId is unique in a store.**

### Run, mode and case metrics are never combined

The three measure different things. `case_complete.elapsedMs` is by S2 definition the sum
of that case's mode elapsed values and excludes discovery; run wall duration is derived
from one-second-resolution stamps. The run wall duration is **not corrected** by summing
modes or cases, a 0 ms value is **not reclassified** as missing, and fractional
milliseconds are never estimated.

To enforce that structurally, every statistics block carries `MetricLevel` and
`MetricResolution`. Run wall duration is always `OneSecond`, and its 0 means "started and
completed within the same second", not "no time passed".

### Each level accumulates its own samples

Rolling dataset → scope → build up by **combining statistics** would produce a mean of
means, which is meaningless. Each level owns a `SampleAccumulator` and sorts and
summarises once at the end.

### Rounding rule

Double summation can vary slightly with order, so reported values are rounded to 6
decimal places (`aggregationRoundMs`). Inputs are untouched; only the printed form is
fixed.

p95 uses nearest rank and is computed and **not hidden** for `n = 1` and `n = 2`, with
its sample count alongside. Whether a sample count justifies a statement is a later
stage's job. With zero eligible samples the statistic **does not exist** (rather than
being 0), and a 0 is a measurement.

### Scope

Regression percentage, thresholds, anomaly judgement, statistical confidence, winner
ranking, resourcePolicy/distance/gpuBackend inference, CLI, GUI, CSV/Markdown reports and
journal schema changes are **all not implemented**.
## 2026-10-01 — S6 Comparison Eligibility design decision

### `(sourceJournalPath, runId)` is the run reference, not runId

S6-4 found `31 accepted runs / 29 distinct runIds`: `suite-ORDER-A/B/C` share one `runId`.
**Identifying a run by `runId` alone keeps one of the three and loses the rest.** That
actually bit while writing S6-5: per-case lookup by `runId` dropped observations, the same
defect that surfaced in S6-4 as 314 -> 324.

The formal run reference is the typed `RunReference { sourceJournalPath, runId }`. A
duplicate of the same `(journal, runId)` is a different question and is already resolved
by S3 recovery semantics; this stage does not re-decide it.

### A candidate is population-versus-population, not a run pairing

When the same condition was repeated N times, **run 1 is not paired against run 1.** Such a
pairing discards the rest of the samples and invents a correspondence the data does not
contain. Each side is a whole aggregate with its own sample count, and the `RunReference`
list behind it exists only for traceability.

`left < right` is fixed by typed key order, so any pair appears once and its sides are the
same on every run.

### Legacy / Unknown provenance is excluded from commit-level comparison

`gitCommitState` is compared **alongside** the `gitCommit` value, so Known, Unknown and
Legacy cohorts are separated structurally. Commit-level comparison requires Known on both
sides.

- **Legacy**: the field does not exist in journals written before it was added.
- **Unknown**: the writer had the field and did not fill it in.
- **Legacy + Legacy** is not treated as the same binary. There is no evidence for it.

One caution: `buildVersion` alone must not settle "same build". The entire point of adding
git provenance in S6-3 was to distinguish different commits under the same app version, so
a Known commit takes precedence. `commitA` vs `commitZ` on the same `0.9.4.43` is a
legitimate pair.

### Unavailable metadata is not treated as "the same conditions"

`distance`, `resourcePolicy` and `gpuBackend` are not in the journal. **Absence is not
agreement.** Not recorded is not the same as matching.

So every candidate carries **nine** `ComparisonLimitations`: distance, resourcePolicy and
gpuBackend unavailable; controlled environment undefined; process isolation uncontrolled;
OS filesystem cache uncontrolled; repeated runs insufficient; run wall one-second
resolution; cancellation unobserved. A bare `comparable=true` with these dropped would be a
claim the data cannot support.

### Candidate generation and regression judgement are separate

This stage decides "may these be compared" and stops there. Regression percentage, speedup
percentage, confidence interval, p-value, threshold pass/fail, winner and better/worse are
**not computed**, and no threshold is chosen, because the OS cache, process isolation,
repeated runs and controlled environment problems remain unsolved.

### `all` stays an independent scope

Only `all vs all` is a candidate, and `all` is never converted to images/videos. §3-2 already
refused to distribute it during aggregation, so comparison follows the same decision.

### CaseElapsed cannot be split by build or mode (structural limit)

S6-4 puts `caseElapsed` on `AggregatedScope` and `AggregatedDataset` but **not** on
`AggregatedBuild`. Case elapsed exists only per dataset+scope; there is no per-build or
per-mode breakdown of it. So a case-elapsed build comparison and a case-elapsed mode
comparison are recorded as `InsufficientData` rather than emitted as candidates whose
numbers do not exist.

The real store already has per-build run wall samples of **1 and 5** in the `images` scope.
Had the Legacy side carried a `gitCommit`, a build-vs-build candidate would exist today.
**Missing provenance is the measured cause of the missing data.**

### A note on state naming

S6-5 eligibility is an **analysis comparability state**, not a benchmark execution status.
It shares no vocabulary with S2's `BenchmarkStatus`, so a cancelled run and an impossible
comparison never look alike. There are nine states: `Eligible` / `MismatchedDataset` /
`MismatchedScope` / `MismatchedMetric` / `MismatchedMode` / `MissingProvenance` /
`SameProvenance` / `NoComparableSamples` / `InsufficientData`.

The order of checks is deliberate too. Dataset identity is verified first, because "a
different dataset" is the more fundamental reason and a caller should not have to satisfy
itself about the other conditions before learning it.

### Scope

Regression percentage, speedup, anomaly, thresholds, confidence, p-value,
winner/better ranking, final reports, CLI, GUI, journal schema changes,
resourcePolicy/distance/gpuBackend inference and timestamp correction are **all not
implemented**.
## 2026-10-01 — CaseElapsed on the build and mode axes (S6-4 structural completion)

### What was missing

S6-4 aggregated `caseElapsed` only onto `AggregatedScope` and `AggregatedDataset`. It was
absent from `AggregatedBuild` and `AggregatedMode`. So S6-5 could not state

```text
same dataset + same scope + build A  vs  build B
```

at case level. The measurement did not exist on that axis; the **axis** did not exist. S6-5
refused with `InsufficientData`, and that record is what exposed the problem.

### A projection, not a new measurement

This completion **creates no new measurement.** It aggregates and preserves the
`case_complete.elapsedMs` values S6-2 had already normalized, along the build and mode axes.
The S6-1/S6-2 normalized meaning is untouched and the existing S6-4 Run/Case/Mode semantics
are unchanged.

The build axis was nearly free: `placeRun()` already fed every case into the dataset, scope
and build cells, and the result was simply **never exposed**. Only the mode axis was new.

### The mode axis is a FILTER, not an allocation (the important decision)

`case_complete.elapsedMs` is by S2 definition the **sum of all of that case's modes**, and
the journal records no split of it. Dividing that total between modes would therefore mean
**inventing a factor that was never measured.** That was refused.

Instead, each mode cohort **filters** to the cases where that mode semantics actually ran.

```text
CPU/CPU   covers the 2 cases where CPU succeeded  -> 100, 200  (mean 150)
AUTO/CPU  covers the 1 case where AUTO succeeded  -> 100         (mean 100)
```

The two populations **overlap by design.** A case where both modes succeeded appears in
both. So these two statistics must **never be added**, and per-file comparison stays the job
of the existing per-file view. The overlap is not hidden: each cohort states it in
`caseAccounting.observed`.

**Skipped contributes nothing.** A `requested=CUDA / effective=CPU / SKIPPED` case is
excluded from that cohort's case population. The S6-4 rule that such a record must not
become a CPU case performance sample is applied unchanged on the case axis.

### The build axis is the sum of that build's scopes

`AggregatedBuild.caseElapsed` and `AggregatedScope.caseElapsed` are **the same samples seen
from two levels.** They are not additive and both hold the same values. The build axis is
used when the question needs them separated by build.

### Real storage: still 0 candidates, which is correct

```text
opportunities  8 -> 11   (three CaseElapsed opportunities added)
eligible           0     (unchanged)
rejected      8 -> 11
  missing-provenance    2 -> 3
  no-comparable-samples 4 -> 8
  insufficient-data     2 -> 0    <- the structural impossibility is gone
```

That `insufficient-data` count falling from 2 to 0 is the evidence the completion worked.
`missing-provenance` took its place: the axis exists and **the commit is still unknown**.

**No gitCommit was backdated onto the Legacy journals to force a candidate.** That shortcut is
forbidden, and backdating would invent provenance the journal never recorded for 30
measurements. Nor was a Known commit synthesised from `buildVersion` alone, nor was
CaseElapsed back-computed from the dataset/scope aggregates, nor was mode elapsed substituted
for case elapsed.

### Two Legacy observations remain true

1. Every case in the `images` scope is **Skipped**, so per-build CaseElapsed has **0**
   samples there. Even if the Legacy side gained a commit, that cohort still has no samples.
2. The `runId` collision (31 accepted / 29 distinct) costs nothing on the build axis: the
   two journals' cases stay separate, and the totals match on both axes.

### Scope

`RunWallDuration` aggregation is **unchanged**: one-second resolution kept, no correction by
mode or case sums, no reclassifying 0 ms as missing. No new statistics algorithm was
introduced (count/min/max/mean/median/p95, 6-decimal rounding, no statistic when eligible is
zero).

Thresholds, winners and better/worse verdicts remain **not implemented**, and none of
5% / 10% / 20% was chosen.
## 2026-10-01 — S6 Comparison Metrics: a computed number is not a verdict

### left/right ordering is not baseline/target

`left < right` from S6-5 is a typed key order, and its whole job is to make the pair
reproducible. **It is not a baseline.** It is not read as `left = old` / `right = new`, and
it is not read as `left = better` / `right = worse`.

An ordering that also implied a direction would quietly **choose** that direction. So
ComparisonMetrics keeps the orientation as a **deterministic order only** and attaches no
public meaning to it. Roles can be assigned later, when a stage lets a user name a baseline
build explicitly.

### A raw comparison is not a regression judgement

```text
absoluteDelta        = right - left                       (ms)
relativeDeltaPercent = ((right - left) / left) * 100
ratio                = right / left
```

`relativeDeltaPercent = +50%` is reported as **+50%**. It is not a regression, an
improvement, better, worse or a winner. Deciding whether a difference matters belongs to a
later decision layer, which does not exist yet. **No threshold is defined here, so pass/fail
is structurally impossible here.**

A test asserts that the layer's vocabulary contains no directional term at all.

### A zero reference makes the ratio and relative delta unavailable

When `left == 0`:

```text
absoluteDelta        = present (computed)
relativeDeltaPercent = unavailable
ratio                = unavailable
```

Neither is replaced with 0, and **no NaN or infinity string is put in the output contract**,
because each of those would be an invented value.

The reason is recorded through the `leftValueIsZero` flag and a `ZeroLeftReference` entry,
so "the ratio is absent because a value was missing" can be told from "the ratio is absent
because the reference was a measured zero". Without that distinction missing and zero look
alike, and the S6-4 rule that a zero is never reclassified as missing would break here.

A `RunWallDuration` of 0 ms in particular is a **real derived value** meaning the two
timestamps fell in the same second. It is an absence of nothing.

### Provenance restricts the calculation

ComparisonMetrics works on the premise that the candidate already passed eligibility, so a
real commit-level candidate is Known against Known. Legacy and Unknown are never converted
to Known, and such a candidate is never generated in the first place, so **there are no
metrics for it either.** A test asserts that.

### The aggregate is consumed, never recomputed

`resolveSide()` borrows the values inside `BenchmarkAggregation` **by pointer**. It copies
nothing and recomputes nothing, so a metric cannot disagree with the aggregate it came from.
It reads no journal, performs no grouping and performs no aggregation.

The nesting level is decided by what is addressed rather than by the dimension alone. A
ModeSemantics comparison and a ModeElapsed metric address a mode cohort; CaseElapsed and
RunWallDuration address the build. A BuildProvenance candidate over ModeElapsed addresses a
mode cohort inside each build, because S6-5 generates it per mode semantics, even though the
dimension says "build".

### Defence in depth

S6-5 already refuses a candidate whose sides disagree on metric level or resolution, and
ComparisonMetrics **re-checks rather than trusting it**, because subtracting numbers from
different metrics is exactly the mistake a delta would hide. On a mismatch nothing is
computed and only the reasons are recorded.

### Statistics are compared independently

`Min / Max / Mean / Median / P95` are each compared on their own. One statistic being
unavailable never removes another statistic's comparison. A test confirms that p95 is not
just the mean repeated: with left values 110 and 120 the p95 is 120.

### Limitations are carried through unchanged

The nine `ComparisonLimitations` from S6-5 are passed through as they are. No second
limitation system was created, and a test pins the count at nine. Nothing is reduced to a
bare `comparable=true`.

### Scope

Thresholds, regression classification, winners, better/worse, confidence intervals,
p-values, statistical significance, anomalies, controlled-environment scores, CLI, GUI,
report formatters, journal schema changes and S2/S3 changes are **all not implemented**.
## 2026-10-01 — S6 Measurement Gate: controlled A/B measurement procedure

Documentation only. Added `docs/implementation-briefs/S6-measurement-gate.ko.md` + `.en.md`.
S6 is **not CLOSED.**

### Existing measurement contracts were reused

No new baseline was invented. Already-measured values were cited.

- `0.9.4.32` **run-to-run variation 3.7-7.5 %** (full runs), **19.4-45.9 %** (short probes)
- `AGENTS.md` item 9: 5 repeats recommended, and "a difference inside measurement error is
  not an improvement"
- S2-PERF's acceptance of the OS filesystem cache and process isolation as **uncontrolled**

> **This is the starting point.** With 5 repeats and 3.7-7.5 % run-to-run variation, **any
> difference below 7.5 % sits inside measurement error** and cannot be declared an
> improvement or a regression. Short probes vary 19-46 %, so adding repeats does not make
> them usable on their own — **the measurement unit itself must not be short.**

### Three findings from the investigation

**1. The current store is not a real dataset.** The case paths point at
`C:\Users\newcl\AppData\Local\Temp\msf_s5_e2e`, which holds **10 files** left over from the
S5 end-to-end test. So `caseMedian 619-645 ms` and `run wall 0 ms` are **properties of a
10-file fixture** and cannot serve as performance evidence.

**2. The GPU is not missing — this is a build configuration issue.** The machine **has an
RTX 3080 Ti**, yet 60 `CUDA -> CPU / SKIPPED` records exist. The cause is the **CPU build**:
the store sits under `build-windows-cpu\Release` and that binary does not link CUDA.

> The interpretation recorded in earlier stages ("a fallback on a machine without GPU
> support") is corrected. The observed values (60 records, SKIPPED) are kept exactly as they
> are; only the reading changes to "the hardware exists and the binary lacked the
> capability." **This is what made GPU independence assumable in the Gate.**

**3. The dataset has zero video files.** Measured extensions show 0 occurrences of `.mp4`,
`.mkv`, `.avi`, `.mov` and `.webm`, and there is no `videos` directory at all. So the
**`videos` scope is impossible for this Gate**, and `all` points at the same file set as
`images`. That fact is recorded in the document.

The real dataset `C:\project\test_sample_img_vid` was confirmed at **3347 files /
102,475,315 bytes / 102 directories**. One `.md` under `format` is not media, so whether it
belongs in the dataset must be confirmed before the Gate; removing it changes the
fingerprint and **both sides must then be re-measured**.

### The procedure that was fixed

| Item | Decision |
| --- | --- |
| Scope | primary `images` (`videos` impossible; `all` equals the `images` file set) |
| Mode | `--mode cpu` **explicitly**. The default `auto,cpu,gpu-max` piles up 260 more Skipped |
| Primary metric | **`ModeElapsed`** |
| Secondary metric | `CaseElapsed` |
| Excluded from primary | **`RunWallDuration`** — one-second resolution; the 21-run cohort's wall median was `0.0` |
| Execution order | crossed `A B B A B B A ...` (cancels linear drift) |
| Cache | **warm adopted as the standard condition.** No OS cache flush, since it affects the whole system |
| Repetition | 5 per build (AGENTS.md item 9). Below 5 is recorded as `INSUFFICIENT`, and statistical sufficiency is never declared |

### The runId collision rule

The CLI's `runId` is `run-YYYYMMDD-HHMM-SS`, **one-second resolution.** So each repeat uses
its **own suite**, passes `--suite` **explicitly**, and starts at least 2 seconds apart.
`RunReference = (sourceJournalPath, runId)` continues to be used.

### Controllable and uncontrollable

| Controllable | Not controllable (kept uncontrolled) |
| --- | --- |
| Power scheme, application internal cache (runtime index separated per suite), background workload (partly), process isolation (partly) | **OS filesystem cache**, scheduler / CPU frequency, turbo / thermal state |

Process isolation and the OS cache are **not presented as controlled.**

### resourcePolicy

There is **no** `--resource` / `--cpu-percent` on the CLI and none in the journal. The Gate
runs on the same machine, same OS session and same power scheme; the resource policy is
stated in the document but **not recorded as a measurement**, and it is not assumed that S6
can later restore it as provenance.

### Gate entry and exit conditions

Discovering a regression is not the success condition. The condition is that data exists with
**2 Known builds + identical dataset/scope/mode + real SUCCESS samples + 5 repeats per build
+ a computed spread + recorded crossed order + recorded environment + S6 candidate > 0**,
verified mechanically with S6's four read-only diagnostics (`known>=2`,
`eligibleCandidates>0`, `absolute deltas available>0`, `missing-provenance=0`,
`no-comparable-samples=0`).

The threshold is **still undefined** and a separate decision stage remains.

### Scope

This stage is **documentation only, with no product code change.** S2 execution, the S3
journal schema, all S6 layers, Scanner, GUI, renderer and CLI were not touched. Benchmark
execution automation, a measurement engine, threshold code, regression code, anomaly code
and a report formatter were not implemented.

While writing the Korean document, two Han characters slipped into the author's own output
against the rule in AGENTS.md item 0. They were found and corrected, and a final scan
confirmed **zero Han characters and zero encoding damage**. The same slip happened a second
time while describing the fix, in a scratch file, before it reached any document.

## 2026-10-01 — External process safety: repeated-spawn ban and bounded lifecycle

Follow-up to the repeating Windows console popup found during S6 measurement. The
cause (3-second throttled `_popen(nvidia-smi)` in `monitor.cpp`, opening and
closing roughly 3000 windows over a 2.7 h run) was already fixed with a one-line
switch to `captureSilent` (`6cc19ba`), and the unfixable-by-stealth nature of the
`WINDOWS_GUI` binary was proven, so Build A was redefined as `5e2b5c1` plus the
fix on a branch commit (`55578d1`). This change addresses the next latent issue:
**unbounded waiting**.

### What changed

- `src/proc_capture.h`: the `WaitForSingleObject(INFINITE)` is gone; every call
  now takes a mandatory caller-chosen `timeoutMs`. No global default exists.
  Telemetry 10000 ms / metadata 30000 ms / decode 120000 ms. On timeout the child
  is terminated, handles are reclaimed, and `false` is returned. The parent never
  waits past the timeout plus a bounded reclamation span.
- Policy applied at all four call sites: `monitor.cpp` (telemetry),
  `video_decoder.cpp` ffprobe (metadata) and single-frame ffmpeg (decode),
  `gui/mainwindow.cpp` `ffprobeSize` (metadata, per-path cache kept).
- The POSIX path keeps `popen` (not a release target). The Windows-only scope is
  stated and the POSIX bound is left as a revisit item.
- Measurement semantics unchanged: same command, same throttle, same fallback
  (cached value kept) on failure. Zero consoles were already achieved by
  `6cc19ba`; this change only bounds the wait.

### Tests

- New `tests/proc_capture_test.cpp`: success, capture (stderr merged), failure,
  empty output, timeout (the case that would hang forever under the old INFINITE
  wait), zero-budget contract. The timeout test cuts a 5 s sleeper with a 1.5 s
  budget and must finish under 5 s.
- `tests/monitor_test.cpp` gains a 20-sample repeated-sampling case: sane return
  plus a 120 s ceiling (GPU leg throttled, so at most the first call can spawn).
- "No console" is not asserted: it cannot be proven by a headless unit test. It
  is guaranteed by construction review (`CREATE_NO_WINDOW`) plus live release-gate
  inspection.

### Rules and documents

- New root `AGENTS.md` item 6 (principles: hot-path repeated-spawn ban,
  run-level isolation allowed, per-call timeout grades, circuit breaker, release
  gate items) and `src_unpacked/AGENTS.md` item 11 (C++ implementation rules).
- No version bump (same precedent as `6cc19ba`), so no `build-history` entry;
  this worklog records it.

### Measurement impact and limits

- No builds or verification runs while R03 is executing (CPU contention would
  contaminate `ModeElapsed`). Code, tests and documents commit first; build,
  CTest, probes and gate verification run in Phase 2 after R03.
- Both A-prime and B share the identical sampling path, so sampling cost cancels
  out of every delta.
- NVML in-process API and a persistent helper stay deferred candidates. Job
  Object tree containment stays a separate decision.

## 2026-10-02 — no-FFmpeg configuration verification and the 083 attempt (measurement incomplete)

Results from the **verification** stage after `e155c8f`. This is not a decision
stage.

### Two no-FFmpeg defects (pre-existing, found now)

Both were the same shape: test code guarded the *declaration* with
`#ifdef MSF_HAS_FFMPEG` but left the **call sites** unguarded. As a result an
`MSF_ENABLE_FFMPEG=OFF` build could not even compile, so the no-FFmpeg
configuration **had never been built before.**

| Defect | File | Commit |
|---|---|---|
| #1 | `tests/video_decode_planner_probe.cpp` — `runDataset` calls `DecodeCounters` / `instrumentedSweep` unguarded | `4670a9d` |
| #2 | `tests/video_sampling_strategy_probe.cpp` — `--hevc-landing` calls `runHevcLanding` unguarded | `bb43774` |

The fix is **only a function/entry-point guard plus a stub**. No backend
redesign and no structural change. Defect #2 surfaced when #1 was rebuilt, and
the build passed after fixing it.

### 082 result (no-FFmpeg)

```text
configure      success
build          success
MSF_ENABLE_FFMPEG      OFF   (verified)
MSF_HAS_FFMPEG in msf_core  absent  (verified -> CLI fallback path is active)
CTest          95/103 passed, 8 failed
```

All 8 are **FFmpeg-dependent tests.**

| Test | exit | Classification |
|---|---|---|
| `video_decode_planner_probe` | 2 | expected skip (explicit message) |
| `video_sampling_strategy_probe` | 2 | expected skip |

does not support the `MSF_ENABLE_FFMPEG=OFF` configuration with a skip/pass
scheme** — CTest treats any non-zero exit as a failure. Kept as follow-up work.

### 083 attempt (not completed)

- `S6MG-083-R01`: aborted by a user kill, journal 2793 lines, **terminal 0**
  -> `incomplete-run`, evidence **preserved** (not overwritten)
- `S6MG-083-R02`: **not started.** deferred for the load problem below
- Provenance had been prepared: fresh build `MSF_BUILD_GIT = bb43774` matching
  HEAD, `MSF_ENABLE_FFMPEG=ON`, `FFMPEG_FOUND=1`, CTest **103/103**

The R03 results (A-prime `55578d1` / B `a3e6eef`, 3334/3334 each,
`ModeElapsed` mean −39.7 ms / −2.06 %) were **not changed.** With one repeat it
remains `INSUFFICIENT`.

### One measurement error (self-correction)

`Get-Counter '\Process(WmiPrvSE*)\% Processor Time'` reported ~300 % on a
single instance, and on that basis I reported "WMI load, 2.9 cores". **That was
wrong.** Re-measured as per-process CPU delta over a 20 s window, `WmiPrvSE`
used **+0.000s (cumulative 0s)**, and WMI client queries in the last 3 minutes
were **0**. Not cross-checking the counter was the cause.

> **Reusable rule:** when attributing system load, do not trust a single
> counter. Check (1) per-process CPU time delta, (2) the user/privileged split
> of `\Processor(_Total)`, and (3) the client pid in the relevant event log.

`taskslinger` (a system monitoring program the user launched) had its WMI
polling genuinely stopped, both instances, with no auto-restart. But it **was not
the source of measurement contamination.**

### The load that actually remained

After the stop, the real system load was **`disk_trim_mover`** (a user program
running disk verification): **66.1 % of one core** over a 20 s window, with a
high kernel-time share, i.e. I/O bound. The user reported it past 55 %, so 083
is deferred until it finishes.

## 2026-10-04 — `--version` redirection misdetection fix + CUDA C4819 removal

Version stays `0.9.4.45` (no bump). Details: `docs/build-history/0.9.4.45.en.md`

### `--version` redirection misdetection

Reported by the user: `MediaSimilarityFinder.exe --version` printed nothing to the
console from PowerShell, while CMD worked.

Decision path: because the executable is GUI subsystem (`WIN32_EXECUTABLE TRUE`),
`GetConsoleWindow()` being null leads to `AttachConsole(ATTACH_PARENT_PROCESS)`.
That path consults `streamIsRedirected()` to decide whether to skip the `CONOUT$`
reopen. The predicate returned `true` for every **unusable** stream: `fd<0`, an
invalid `_get_osfhandle` result (`-1`/`0`), and `FILE_TYPE_UNKNOWN`.

So a PowerShell launch whose `stdout`/`stderr` were not real output targets was
classified as redirected, `AttachConsole` was skipped, and `std::cout` had
nowhere to write — hence no `--version` output. CMD took the console-handle path
and was unaffected.

The fix was to return `false` for those three cases. Only a genuinely usable
`FILE_TYPE_DISK`/`FILE_TYPE_PIPE` counts as redirected, so the original design
intent — preserve real redirection — is kept and only the misdetection is
removed (`gui/main.cpp:41-49`).

### A separate constraint found during verification (not a regression)

`--version > file` yields 0 bytes from PowerShell. It **reproduces identically on
the pre-fix binary** and leaves `$LASTEXITCODE` empty. The cause is that PowerShell
does not wait for GUI-subsystem executables; this change did not introduce it. OS
level redirection (`cmd /c "exe --version > file"`) and
`Start-Process -Wait -RedirectStandardOutput` both record correctly. Console
output verification should therefore use OS level redirection as the criterion.

### CUDA C4819

The `warning C4819` in the GPU build log was not a CUDA syntax error but an
encoding warning: code page 949 cannot represent non-ASCII characters in the
CUDA headers. Cause: `/utf-8` was applied to `CXX` only and never reached the
CUDA host compiler.

`nvcc` does not accept `/utf-8` directly, so it is forwarded to the MSVC host
compiler via `-Xcompiler`. The first attempt used `COMPILE_LANG_AND_ID:CUDA,MSVC`
and **failed to match, because CUDA reports compiler id `NVIDIA`**. Switching to
the `COMPILE_LANGUAGE:CUDA` + `CXX_COMPILER_ID:MSVC` combination puts
`-Xcompiler="/EHsc -Ob2 /utf-8"` on the nvcc command line. A forced recompile
reported C4819=0, warning=0, error=0.

### Boundaries of this step

```text
CMakeLists.txt             added /utf-8 for the CUDA host compiler
gui/main.cpp               corrected the streamIsRedirected predicate
version bump               none (stays 0.9.4.45)
CPU CTest                  102/102 PASS
GPU CTest                  103/103 PASS
dedicated console-output regression test   not added (recorded as a candidate)
S4 / S5 / S6 / NVDEC      kept DEFERRED
```

### Product defects found (DEFECT-A, DEFECT-B)

Dataset: `C:\project\test_sample_img_vid\images` (707 files = 706 media + 1 `.md`)

**Defective file: `images/format/tiff/ycbcr_lzw_bt709.tif` (146,356 bytes)**

#### DEFECT-A — a decode failure is silently indexed

- Reproduction: put that single file in a folder and run the product `--scan`; it
  reproduces every time.
- Production path: `MediaSearchEngine::scan()` -> `MediaPipeline::analyze()` ->
  `ImageDecoder` (WIC). This is the confirmed production path, not an auxiliary one.
- Observed: `scanned=1 added=1 analyzed=0 candidates=0 groups=0`
- Impact scope: CPU and GPU fail identically (so parity holds). The file remains in
  the DB as a `files` row but has **no fingerprint, so it participates in no
  comparison or search result.**
- User exposure: **no warning or error on stdout/stderr at all.** exit=0, so it
  looks like a success. On a full-dataset scan it is only visible as
  `analyzed=693` being one lower than `scanned=694`.
- CPU/GPU parity: both trees report `analyzed=0` — identical behavior.

#### DEFECT-B — a file that never analyzes is reported as `modified` forever

- Reproduction: after it is indexed under DEFECT-A, rescan the same folder.
- Observed (4 consecutive runs, measured):
  ```
  run1: added=1     modified=0 analyzed=0
  run2: added=0     modified=1 analyzed=0
  run3: added=0     modified=1 analyzed=0
  run4: added=0     modified=1 analyzed=0
  ```
- Impact scope: a file whose analysis fails **never converges to `unchanged` and
  stays `modified=1` on every scan.** `modified` means "queued for reanalysis", so
  the counter contradicts reality and the scan report is permanently inaccurate in
  the same way.
- No reanalysis cost is actually incurred (`analyzed=0`), so this is **not a
  performance problem; it is a report-accuracy and state-convergence problem.**

### What the existing tests miss

- `ycbcr_lzw` and `bt709` appear **0 times** across `tests/`. The file exists in
  the dataset yet no regression covers it.
- `analyze_telemetry_test.cpp:137` verifies "undecodable paths never report a cache
  hit", but that is telemetry-scoped; it does **not** verify the report counters
  (`modified`/`analyzed`) or scan convergence.
- **There is no test asserting that a rescan converges to `unchanged` when a file
  fails analysis.** That gap is what let DEFECT-B pass.
- `search_engine_test` calls `openIndex(dbPath)` directly and forces GPU off with
  `if(e.gpuActive())return 17;`, so it verifies neither the production entry point
  (`openIndexForRoot`) nor GPU parity. The production entry point is covered by
  `match_revalidate_test` / `video_scan_e2e_test` / `index_manager_test` /
  `scan_streaming_test` / `walker_queue_test` / `dataset_e2e_test` /
  `video_sampling_e2e_test`.
- Skipped unsupported extensions (12 `.ico` files) are also not reported anywhere.
  The allowlist is hardcoded at `src/scanner.cpp:15,21` and `.ico` is absent.

## 2026-10-05 — 0.9.4.46 DEFECT-A/B fix (queue 0 and 1 complete)

Detail: `docs/build-history/0.9.4.46.en.md`

### Cause: the two defects were not independent bugs

They were judged to be two symptoms of a single missing failure state model.

`processOne()` in `MediaSearchEngine::scan()` used `fingerprint==0` to express
both **"analysis not completed (retry needed)"** and **"analysis failed (no retry
needed)"**, and no field separated them.

- **DEFECT-A**: `added`/`modified` were counted **before** analysis, so a file
  with no fingerprint was reported as successfully indexed
- **DEFECT-B**: `fingerprint==0` made `changed` unconditionally true, so a failed
  file was reported as `modified=1` on every scan while no reanalysis actually
  happened (leaving `analyzed=0`)

-> Fixed as one state transition.

### State model adopted

A `files.analysis_failed` column (default 0) separates the two meanings of
`fingerprint==0`.

| fingerprint | analysis_failed | meaning | retry |
|---|---|---|---|
| != 0 | 0 | analysis completed | not needed |
| 0 | 0 | skeleton (cancel/crash/not reached) | **needed** |
| 0 | 1 | attempted, no fingerprint produced | **not needed** while content is unchanged |

`added`/`modified` moved to analysis **outcome** time and a `failed` counter was
introduced. Failures are surfaced through the CLI, the GUI, telemetry, and the
benchmark journal, and telemetry `pending` became `scanned - analyzed - failed` so
a failed file is no longer misread as outstanding work.

### Fixture decision

As directed, it was judged first whether the real TIFF is strictly required. It is
**not**. The defect is a state transition, not a format, so a single 64x64 BMP
header carrying no pixel data reproduces it deterministically. Nothing hardcodes
a file name or a TIFF subtype.

### Confirmed the regression test actually catches the defect

Removing `&& !analysisFailed` from `pendingAnalysis` to restore DEFECT-B behavior
makes the new test **exit 1** (three convergence checks fail). After restoring, all
pass.

> **Reusable rule**: after restoring a source file, always raise its mtime to force
> recompilation. `Copy-Item` preserves the source `LastWriteTime`, so make skips the
> rebuild, the `.obj` stays at the previous state, and tests fail for no real reason.
> This actually happened during this task.

> **Reusable rule (test design)**: a regression test must verify **invariants**, not
> "the file that triggered the bug". Here it is anchored on the accounting identity
> `scanned == added + modified + unchanged + failed` plus identical reports from the
> third and fourth scans. Pinning individual counter values would break whenever a
> legitimate improvement lands on the normal path.

### Measured results

```
CPU Release CTest  103/103 PASS   (previous 102 + 1 new)   warning 0 / error 0
GPU Release CTest  104/104 PASS   (previous 103 + 1 new)   warning 0 / C4819 0
new test analysis_failure_state_test  28 checks  PASS on both CPU and GPU
```

Normal-semantics preservation, fresh index over the 14 files in `format/tiff`:
```
before : scanned=14 added=14 analyzed=13 candidates=3 groups=3
after  : scanned=14 added=13 analyzed=13 failed=1  candidates=3 groups=3   CPU == GPU
rescan : scanned=14 unchanged=14 analyzed=0 failed=0 candidates=3 groups=3
```
`candidates`/`groups` are **unchanged**, which is the measured proof that
Search/Index/Comparison verdicts did not move.

The full 694-file dataset is also identical on CPU/GPU (`candidates=174 groups=169`
retained), and the file that repeated as `modified=1` during acceptance is now
reported once as `failed=1` and then converges.

### Not done in this build

`color_thumb` R1, XMP coverage validation, S4 real-screen acceptance, the S5
benchmark, the S6 gate, and unsupported-extension transparency all remain
follow-up tasks. **Unsupported-extension transparency was found during acceptance
but sits outside this directive's scope, so it is only registered in the queue and
not implemented.**

### Versions

`0.9.4.45` -> `0.9.4.46`. DB schema `1.0.3` -> `1.0.4` (additive column).
`kEngineVersion 1.5.0` / `kBenchmarkSchemaVersion 9` / `kCacheFormatVersion 9` are
kept, because the counter meanings for normal files are untouched and the verdict
version was not raised.
